author: Old Dominion News
title: Virginia men's golf team enters ACC Championship as top seed
text:
The Virginia men’s golf team will enter the 2026 Atlantic Coast Conference (ACC) Championship as the top seed, according to an announcement on April 22. The championship’s three-day, 54-hole stroke play portion is set to begin Thursday, with the top eight teams advancing to match play on Sunday.
The event holds significance for participating schools as it determines standings and rivalries within the conference. For Virginia, earning the number one seed reflects its strong performance leading up to the tournament.
The semifinals and finals of the ACC Men’s Golf Championship match play will be televised live on ACCNX starting Sunday at approximately 2 p.m. Eastern Time and concluding Monday at 10 a.m. A recap show is scheduled for May 10 at 11 a.m. on ACCN. Ryan Burr will provide play-by-play commentary alongside analyst Steve Scott.
Teams will compete in three rounds of stroke play—18 holes each day from Thursday through Saturday—before moving into match play quarterfinals and semifinals on Sunday and a final round Monday. This year’s championship takes place at Shark’s Tooth Golf Course in Naples, Florida, a par-72 course measuring 7,246 yards that features mature trees, undulating greens, deep bunkers, pine forest views, and proximity to Lake Powell.
Virginia’s lineup includes Ben James, Paul Chang, Bryan Lee, Josh Duangmanee, and Michael Lee. The tournament field features fifteen teams seeded by their rankings as of April 15: Virginia (1), North Carolina (2), Stanford (3), Georgia Tech (4), Florida State (5), Duke (6), Notre Dame (7), Wake Forest (8), Clemson (9), Louisville (10), SMU (11), NC State (12), California (13), Virginia Tech (14) and Boston College (15).
Additionally, this event factors into the Smithfield Commonwealth Clash—a points-based rivalry between UVA and Virginia Tech where annual head-to-head results determine which school claims the Commonwealth Clash trophy.
